text: Tɛnɛndo, Stanford kɛnɛya sanfɛkalanso donnikɛbaw ye baana sƐgƐ sƐgƐli minan kura do dilani kumalase min ni a be se ka seliliw suguya woloma: pisi fitifitinin do min  bese ka dilan ni Ɛnpirmanti ankirima ye US wari tama ɲɔgɔnna a kelen o kelen songɔ ye .
eng_text: On Monday, scientists from the Stanford University School of Medicine announced the invention of a new diagnostic tool that can sort cells by type: a tiny printable chip that can be manufactured using standard inkjet printers for possibly about one U.S. cent each.

text: Ɲinninikɛla jɔnjɔnw  ko ko o be se ka to boɔ bana, Sɔgɔsɔgɔnijɛ, SIDA bana ani Sumaya sƐgƐsƐgƐli joona ka se ka kƐ banabatɔw dɛsɛbato jamana la, yɔrɔ minw na ni boɔbanatɔ inafɔ sin na boɔ balota hakƐ bese ka dɔgɔya ni setigi jamanaw ta tila.
eng_text: Lead researchers say this may bring early detection of cancer, tuberculosis, HIV and malaria to patients in low-income countries, where the survival rates for illnesses such as breast cancer can be half those of richer countries.

text: LajƐba in daminƐra taalen nƐgƐ kaɲƐ 11 waati, ye leri la (UTC +1), Whiteall kan, ka ɲƐsin dodaba ma min kɔlɔsilen tun be Downing Street polosiw fƐ, minisiri ɲƐmɔgɔ ka fama sigiyɔrɔ.
eng_text: The protest started around 11:00 local time (UTC+1) on Whitehall opposite the police-guarded entrance to Downing Street, the Prime Minister's official residence.

text: 11:00 tƐmƐra drɔn, mamurutilenw ye sira tigƐ kƐɲƐkan fƐ siraba kan Whitehall kɔnɔ.
eng_text: Just after 11:00, protesters blocked traffic on the northbound carriage in Whitehall.

text: 11 h 20 waati, polosiw  ye a ɲinnin lajƐkƐbaw  ko u ka segin sirakƐrƐfƐ dali kan, ka a jiraw la ka kakan u ka murutili hakƐ ni taa – ni – ka – segin fangaboɲali jateminƐ ka bƐrƐbƐn.
eng_text: At 11:20, the police asked the protesters to move back on to the pavement, stating that they needed to balance the right to protest with the traffic building up.

text: Taalen 11 h 29 waati , lajƐ taarase fɔ Whitehall kan, ka tƐmƐ Trafalgar Square fƐ, fo Strand, ka tƐmƐ  Aldwych fƐ ani ka  yƐlƐn Kingsway fƐ ka i kunsi Holborn ma min  ni kɔnseriwateriw ka polotikitɔn be a ka tilemafƐ ɲɔgɔnnajƐrƐ ke Grand Connaught Rooms dunanjigiso la.
eng_text: Around 11:29, the protest moved up Whitehall, past Trafalgar Square, along the Strand, passing by Aldwych and up Kingsway towards Holborn where the Conservative Party were holding their Spring Forum in the Grand Connaught Rooms hotel.

eng_text: "Panama Papers" is an umbrella term for roughly ten million documents from Panamanian law firm Mossack Fonseca, leaked to the press in spring 2016.

text: SƐbƐn olu ye a jira ko waribɔ tan ni naani ye sannikƐla nafolotigibaw dƐmƐ ka Ameriki dolari waari miliyari caman dogo yasa ka kisi nisɔngɔ ani sariyawƐrƐw ma.
eng_text: The documents showed fourteen banks helped wealthy clients hide billions of US dollars of wealth to avoid taxes and other regulations.

text: Britanikiw ka kunafonigafƐ The Guardian ye a do maw kun na ko Deutsche warimaraso tun be a janto cakƐda guwansan 1200  tila sabanan na minw tun talen do ni ka nin ko in kƐli kan ma.
eng_text: British newspaper The Guardian suggested Deutsche Bank controlled roughly a third of the 1200 shell companies used to accomplish this.

eng_text: There were protests worldwide, several criminal prosecutions, and the leaders of the governments of Iceland and Pakistan both resigned.

eng_text: As the cars ahead of Alonso went in for fuel under the safety car, he moved up the pack to take victory.

text: Kĩbindi kĩa PBS kĩna ngerenwa cia Emmy itanyihĩire mirongo ĩrĩ na inya, na nĩ gĩkuhĩ kurĩ Saseme Street na Mister Roger's Neighborhood.
eng_text: The PBS show has more than two-dozen Emmy awards, and its run is shorter only than Sesame Street and Mister Rogers' Neighborhood.

text: O kihingo gia kĩbindi kĩu nĩkĩahinyagĩrĩria ũndũ ũmwe ibukuinĩ rĩmwe na gĩkatabania ũhoro ũcio na ng'ano nyingĩ.
eng_text: Each episode of the show would focus on a theme in a specific book and then explore that theme through multiple stories.

text: Kĩbindi nokiaheaga ciana mwerekera wa mabuku marĩa cigwetha na cithome rĩrĩa ciathiĩ library.
eng_text: Each show would also provide recommendations for books that children should look for when they went to their library.

text: John Grant, kuuma WNED Buffalo (kĩhumo kĩa Reading Rainbow) augire "Reading Rainbow yathomithagia ciana gĩtumi gĩa gũthoma,... wendo wa gũthoma -[kĩbindi kĩu] kĩendithagĩrĩa ciana kuoya ibuku na kũrĩthoma."
eng_text: John Grant, from WNED Buffalo (Reading Rainbow's home station) said "Reading Rainbow taught kids why to read,... the love of reading — [the show] encouraged kids to pick up a book and to read."

text: Hamwe na John Grant, amwe metĩkĩtie atĩ ũnyihu wa mĩcara na ũgarũrũku wa mwĩcirĩrie wa gĩthomo kĩa tafaarĩra nĩgĩcangĩire gũthira kwa kĩbindi kĩu.
eng_text: It is believed by some, including John Grant, that both the funding crunch and a shift in the philosophy of educational television programming contributed to ending the series.

text: Fiyɛnkoloba, min be fo 'mayili' 645 (kilomɛtɛrɛ 1040) Cap Vert jamana tilebin bolo kan, ina fɔ min bena jɛnsɛn yani ka dugukolo yɔrɔ tɔw kasara, waatijateminɛnlaw ko te.
eng_text: The storm, situated about 645 miles (1040 km) west of the Cape Verde islands, is likely to dissipate before threatening any land areas, forecasters say.

text: Sisan Fred mumuko ye 'mayili' 105 nɛgɛ kanɲɛ kelen kɔnɔ, w'a be k'a ɲɛsin worodugutilebin seleke la
eng_text: Fred currently has winds of 105 miles per hour (165 km/h) and is moving towards the northwest.

text: Fred ye kɔkɔjiba jamanaw bɛɛ la fiyɛnkolo la fagamaba de ye min ɲɔngɔn ma ye fo bii Atlantik kɔkɔjii kɔrɔn n'a tile bin na kabini satelite jaama nana, ani kɔkɔjida fiyɛnkoloba saaban min lakodonnen do kɔrɔn fƐ ni 35°W hakƐ.
eng_text: Fred is the strongest tropical cyclone ever recorded so far south and east in the Atlantic since the advent of satellite imagery, and only the third major hurricane on record east of 35°W.

text: Sɛtanburu kalo tile 24 san 1759 Arthur Guinness ye bolonɔ da singa san 9000 St James Gate Brewery Dublin Irland jamanan ye.
eng_text: On September 24, 1759, Arthur Guinness signed a 9,000 year lease for the St James' Gate Brewery in Dublin, Ireland.

text: San 250 kɔfɛ, Guinness ye sɔrɔcakɛ yiriwa min be munumun Euro wari kasabi miliyari 10 ( America jamanan Wari dollari 14) san o san.
eng_text: 250 years later, Guinness has grown to a global business that turns over 10 billion euros (US$14.7 billion) every year.

text: Jonny Reid, New Zealand pakurubilola tɔɲɔgon A1GP kulu la, dona tariku la sabu a ye pankuruboli bɛɛ la telima kɛ ka tƐmƐ Auckland Harbour babili kan, min sii be san 48 na, siriya la.
eng_text: Jonny Reid, co-driver for the A1GP New Zealand team, today made history by driving the fastest over the 48-year-old Auckland Harbour Bridge, New Zealand, legally.

text: Mr Reid sera ka New Zealand A1GP mɔbili, Black beauty boli k'a tɛmɛ km 160 kan nɛgɛ kanɲɛ kelen kɔnɔ babili in sanfɛ siyɛn wolowila
eng_text: Mr Reid managed to drive the New Zealand's A1GP car, Black Beauty at speeds over 160km/h seven times over the bridge.

text: New Zealand lakanatigilamɔgɔw ye gɛlɛya sɔrɔ walasa ka Mr Reid ka boli teliya suma ni teliyasumanikɛlaw ye bawu Black Beauty ka surun, tuma kelen min na u sera ka Mr Reid ka boli teliya suma o kɛra waati minna a bolila km 160 kan nɛgɛ kanɲɛ kelen kɔnɔ
eng_text: The New Zealand police had trouble using their speed radar guns to see how fast Mr Reid was going because of how low Black Beauty is, and the only time the police managed to clock Mr Reid was when he slowed down to 160km/h.

text: Kalo 3 tɛmɛnen in na, a ka ciya ni mɔgɔ minɛnlen 80 ye minnu labilala ka bɔ Central Booking kaso la k'a sɔr'u ma ɲagi kɛnɛkan
eng_text: In the last 3 months, over 80 arrestees were released from the Central Booking facility without being formally charged.

text: Ni san Awirili kalo la, waati kunkuru minɛli yamaruya bɔra kiiritigɛla Glynn fɛ k'a ɲɛsin koso in ma walasa ka mɔgɔw labila minnu datugulendon a ka ciya min nɛgɛ kanɲɛ 24 ye u ka minɛli kɔfɛ n'u ma lamɛ kiiritigɛba dɔ fɛ
eng_text: In April this year, a temporary restaining order was issued by Judge Glynn against the facility to enforce the release of those held more than 24 hours after their intake who did not receive a hearing by a court commissioner.

text: Kiiritigɛla in be musaga dɔ sigi sen  kan, ni jɛn kɛr'a ma, w'a be ɲaginliw sɛbɛntiya minɛlikɛla ɲɛmɔgɔ fɛ. Ɲangiliw be don jamana ka ɔridinatɛrɛ ɲɛsiraw fɛ, min b'a to kiri in be se ka sirabɔ.
eng_text: The commissioner sets bail, if granted, and formalizes the charges filed by the arresting officer. The charges are then entered into the state's computer system where the case is tracked.

text: Lamɛli in be siganamɔgɔ in ka hakɛ don tamaseren ka kiiri lateliya.
eng_text: The hearing also marks the date for the suspect’s right to a speedy trial.

text: Peter Costello Australia waribon tigi ye mɔgɔ min ka teli ka na Minisiri ɲɛmɔgɔ John Howard nɔna ka sabu kɛ Liberal Party ton y'a ka dɛmɛ di nikiliyɛr goni dilanyɔrɔko ma Australia
eng_text: Peter Costello, Australian treasurer and the man most likely to succeed Prime Minister John Howard as Liberal party leader has thrown his support behind a nuclear power industry in Australia.

text: Mr Costello ko tuma minna nikiliyɛri goni labɛnni be se ka kɛ wariko sira fɛ, Australia ka kan ka se tɛmɛ  n'a jenini ye
eng_text: Mr Costello said that when nuclear power generation becomes economically viable, Australia should pursue its use.

text: "N'a kɛra jagoko ye, an ka kan ka sɔrɔ. O kɔrɔ ye, balili jonjon sarati te nikiliyɛri goni la" Mr Costello y'a fɔ.
eng_text: "If it becomes commercial, we should have it. That is, there's no in-principle objection to nuclear energy" Mr Costello said.

text: Ansa ka fɔ la, "lakanatigilamɔw sen be gosili kankara damadɔ la w'u sirannen do o kana fanga yɛlɛma kɛlɛ dɔ bange.
eng_text: According to Ansa, "police were concerned by a couple of top-level hits they feared might spark a full-blown war of succession.

text: Lakanatigilamɔgɔw ko Lo Piccolo bolo ka jan bari a kun kɛra Provenzan dɛmɛ bolo dɔ ye w'a  ka kodon ba ye boɲan s'a ma ka bɔ kɔrɔ famaw yɔrɔ k'a d'a kan u ye Provenzan ka marakɛcogo dɔgoya f'a dan k'a sɔrɔ ku ka fanga jurusira sinsin
eng_text: Police said Lo Piccolo had the upper hand because he had been Provenzano's right-hand man in Palermo and his greater experience won him the respect of the older generation of bosses as they pursued Provenzano's policy of keeping as low as possible while strengthening their power network.

text: Ni fama nunu tun marala Provenzano fɛ tuma minn'a ye dan siri Rinna ka kɛlɛ kolokolonen la ka ɲɛ sin jamana in ma  min ye Mafia kɛlɛkɛdenw Giovanni Falcone ni Paolo Borsellino dajili laɲini san 1992.
eng_text: These bosses had been reined in by Provenzano when he put an end to the Riina-driven war against the state that claimed the lives of Mafia crusaders Giovanni Falcone and Paolo Borsellino in 1992."

eng_text: Brazil is the largest Roman Catholic country on Earth, and the Roman Catholic Church has consistently opposed the legalization of same-sex marriage in the country.

text: O Kɔfɛ, a bɔlen kɛnɛkan ko di caman tun be ka dɛmɛ ɲini sariyala yasa ka uka wuliliw bali, ɲɔgɔnye dɔ tun kɛra Marisikalo tile 20 East Bay Law Community Center la so ŋanamulen tigiw kan
eng_text: After it became apparent that many families were seeking legal help to fight the evictions, a meeting was held on March 20 at the East Bay Community Law Center for the victims of the housing scam.

text: Lockwood Gardens sotigi minw  dalen bƐ a la ko  du 40 walima min ka ca oye bƐ se ka lawili kabini u ya mɛn ko OHA lpolɔsiw fana bƐ ka ɲinini kɛ foroba so wɛrɛw kan Oakland minw be se ka sɔrɔ so ŋanamuŋanaulenw in na.
eng_text: Tenants at Lockwood Gardens believe that there may be another 40 families or more to face eviction, since they learned that OHA police are also investigating other public housing properties in Oakland that may be caught up in the housing scam.

text: Gɛrɛki soronnadoba lakodɔnnenw ninnu, Sakis Kechagioglou ni Nikolakopoulos datugura Athen Korydallus kaso la ka da a kan u  sɔrɔla surɔfɛn ni yuruguyurugu la.
eng_text: The famous Greek lawyers, Sakis Kechagioglou and George Nikolakopoulos have been imprisoned in the Athens' jail of Korydallus, as they were found guilty of graft and corruption.

text: lasɔmiseni bɛ foko ji sanfɛ ka da sanfɛla fanga ye.

text: dakunfila bɛ sisan sanbɛlɛbolinɛgɛ la digankurulen bɛ munu ni ɲɔkɔn cɛ. dadumanfilaw bɛ sanbɛlɛw famuya ka ɲɛ, ali ni jɛnkɛnni kɛla.
eng_text: The blade on a modern ice skate has a double edge with a concave hollow between them. The two edges allow for a better grasp of the ice, even when tilted.

text: k'a sabu kɛ nɛgɛ kɔfɛla tikɛlen do dɔni, ka nɛgɛ jɛnkɛnlen to fan dɔ fɛ walima dɔ wɛrɛ fɛ, dakun min dalen do sanbɛlɛ kan bɛ kuru fɛnɛ.
eng_text: Because the bottom of the blade is slightly curved, as the blade tilts to one side or the other, the edge which is in contact with the ice also curves.

text: o bɛ sanbɛlɛbolikɛla bila ka fara. ni sanbɛlɛbolifɛn jɛnkɛnna kinin fɛ, sanbɛlɛbolikɛla bɛ jɛnkɛn kinin fɛ, ni sanbɛlɛbolifɛn jɛnkɛnna numan fɛ, sanbɛlɛbolikɛla bɛ jɛnkɛn numan fɛ.
eng_text: This causes the skater to turn. If the skates tilt to the right, the skater turns right, if the skates tilt to the left, the skater turns left.

text: Walasa k'u funtenikɔrɔ labɔ, u ka kan ka u funtenikurafaralen de labɔ u ye min sɔrɔ yeelen fɛ.
eng_text: To return to their previous energy level, they must get rid of the extra energy they got from the light.

text: u kɛtɔla k'o kɛ u bɛ yeelen fitini dɔ fili min tɔkɔ ye "photon" ye.

text: triceratope ɲinw tɛ furaburuw durɔn ɲimi nka jiribolokolojalenw ani ndiliw.

eng_text: Some scientists think Triceratops ate cycads, which are a type of plant that was common in the Cretaceous.

eng_text: A person who weighs 200 pounds (90kg) on Earth would weigh about 36 pounds (16kg) on Io. So the gravity, of course, pulls less on you.

text: a bɛ san baasaba bɔ kɔ, san 1610, dugukolokoɲɛɲinikɛla ka bɔ Italie Galileo Galilei ye jateminɛ kɛ telescope la ka ye ko kɛrɛw bɛ Venus la, i n'a fɔ kalo.
eng_text: About three thousand years later, in 1610, Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei used a telescope to observe that Venus has phases, just as the moon does.

text: kɛrɛw bɛ kɛ yi k'a d'a kan Venus fanmi durɔn (walima kalo ta) sinna Tile ma jɛlen do. Venus kɛrɛw jateminɛna  Copernicus hakilina fɛ min ko dugukolow bɛ Tile munumunu.
eng_text: Phases happen because only the side of Venus (or of the Moon) facing the Sun is lighted. The phases of Venus supported the theory of Copernicus that the planets go around the Sun.

text: Ola, san daman-daman o kɔ 1639 san, Angilɛ dugukolokoɲɛɲinikɛla min tɔgɔ ye Jeremiah Horrocks ye Venus yɛlɛma-yɛlɛma jateminɛ.
eng_text: Then, a few years later in 1639, an English astronomer named Jeremiah Horrocks observed a transit of Venus.

eng_text: He originally named the Hangeul alphabet Hunmin Jeongeum, which means "the correct sounds for the instruction of the people".

text: Hakilinasira caman be ka jira  Sanskrit bɔra cogo minna. U dɔ la kelen ye ko Aryan dɔ ka taali senfɛ k'a bɔ Ɛndi jamana tilebin fɛ a taara ni kan in y'a bolo.
eng_text: There are many theories to how Sanskrit came into existence. One of them is about an Aryan migration from the west into India who brought their language with them.

eng_text: The earliest known book in the world was written in Sanskrit. After the compilation of Upanishads, Sanskrit just faded due to hierarchy.

text: Sanskrit kan ka misɛn ani kan   nafama do, min kɛra Ɛndi kaw ka kan kura caman ju ye, inafɔ Latɛn kɛra Erɔpu kanw ju ye inafɔ Faransi kan ani Ɛsipaɲi kan.
eng_text: Sanskrit is a very complex and rich language, which has served to be the source for many modern Indian languages, just like Latin is the source for European languages like French and Spanish.

text: Faransi kunkan kɛlɛ in bannen, Alimaɲi Jamana y'a labɛn ka Biritaɲi ka Iziland minɛn.
eng_text: With the battle for France over, Germany began to get ready to invade the island of Britain.

text: Alimaɲi ye kɛlɛ in tɔgɔ dogolen da ko ''Kɔkɔjiwara kɛlɛwale''. Biritaɲi kɛlɛbolo maramafɛn girimanw ni balow fanba ciyɛnna uka  Dunkirk bɔli senfɛ, wa kɛlɛbolo in fɛgɛyara kosɛbɛ.

text: Nka hali ola Royal Navy Kɛlɛbolo tun ka farin kosebe  k'a tɛmɛ Alimaɲi Navy Kɛlɛbolo kan (''Kriegsmarine'') ani a tun be se ka firinkan jikankɛlɛkɛla bɛɛ siban ka bɔ Angilɛ kaw ka Dugumasira fɛ.

text: Nka, Royal Navy kɛlɛbolo jikurun damadɔ dɔrɔn tun dagalen do  firinkan nasira kɛrɛfɛ sabu adimiraliw tun siranna u kana ciyɛn Alimaɲi fiyɛnkɛlɛbolo binkan dɔ fɛ.
eng_text: However, very few Royal Navy ships were based near the likely invasion routes as the admirals were afraid they would be sunk by German air attack.

text: An ka daminɛ ni ɲɛfɔli dɔ ye Itali ka laɲini kan. Kɛrɛnkɛnrɛnnenyala Itali tun ye Alimaɲi ni Zapɔn ''dɔgɔcɛ'' ye.
eng_text: Let's start with an explanation about Italy's plans. Italy was mainly the "little brother" of Germany and Japan.

text: Kɛlɛbolo  ni jikankɛlɛbolo fangabannen tun b'a fɛ, k'a sɔrɔ u tun bɔra ka jikurun naani dilan yani kɛlɛ in ka daminɛ.
eng_text: It had a weaker army and a weaker navy, although they had just built four new ships right before the beginning of the war.

text: Itali ka laɲini fanba tun ye Farafinna jamanaw ye. Walasa ko jamanaw sɔrɔ, u tun mako be kɛlɛkulu dɔ ciyɔrɔ la walasa kɛlɛkuluw ka se ka Mediterane kɔkɔji cɛci ka Farafinna minɛn.
eng_text: Italy's main goals were African countries. To capture those countries, they would need to have a troop launching pad, so as troops could sail across the Mediterranean Sea and invade Africa.

text: O kɔson, u tun kakan k'u tila Biritaɲi ka kɛlɛdakayɔrɔw ni jikurun la Ezipiti. O waleya nunuw kɛrɛfɛ, Itali ka kɛlɛkɛ jikɛlɛkɛkurunw tun bisikiyalen te ka foyi wɛrɛ kɛ.
eng_text: For that, they had to get rid of British bases and ships in Egypt. Besides those actions, Italy's battleships were not supposed to do anything else.

text: Sisan Zapɔn ka ko la. Zapɔn tun ye gun jamana dɔ ye inafɔ Biritaɲi.
eng_text: Now for Japan. Japan was an island country, just like Britain.

text: jijukɔrɔkurunw ye jikurunw ye minnuw kɛrɛnkɛrɛnnen do ji jukɔrɔ boli la ani k'u kɛ yen  waati jan kɔnɔ.
eng_text: Submarines are ships designed to travel underwater, and remain there for an extended amount of time.

text: jijukɔrɔkurunw labaarala Diyɛn Kɛlɛba I ni Diyɛn Kɛlɛba Il senfɛ. O waati u tun ka suma ani u ka muguci kuntaala tun ka surun.
eng_text: Submarines were used in World War I and World War II. Back then they were very slow and had a very limited shooting range.

text: Kɛlɛ in daminɛ la u tun be taama fanba kɛ kɔkɔji sanfɛ,  nka tuma minna jateminɛn-mansin yiriwala ka jaw jɛ jijukɔrɔkurunw jagoyala ka don jijukɔrɔ walasa k'u yeli bali.
eng_text: In the beginning of the war they mostly travelled on top of the sea, but as radar began developing and becoming more accurate the submarines were forced to go under water to avoid being seen.

text: Alimaɲi jijukɔrɔkurunw tun be wele ko U-Boats. Alimaɲi kaw tun be se kɔsɛbɛ jijukɔrɔkurun bolili n'a lataama cogo la.
eng_text: German submarines were called U-Boats. The Germans were very good at navigating and operating their submarines.

text: Ka d'uka jijukɔrɔkurun ɲɛtaa kan, kɛlɛ in kɔfɛ  dannaya t'a kan ni jijukɔrɔkurun cama te Alimaɲikaw bolo.
eng_text: Because of their success with submarines, after the war Germans aren't trusted to have many of them.

text: Awɔ! Masa Tutankhamun, min tun be  wele tuma dɔw la ko "Masa Tut" walima "Masa Cɛni", ye Izipiti kɔrɔ  Masa dɔnnen ba dɔ ye waati kura nunu na.
eng_text: Yes! King Tutankhamun, sometimes referred to as "King Tut" or "The Boy King", is one of the most well known ancient Egyptian kings in modern times.

text: A kaɲi a ka fɔ k'a tun m'a jate kaɲɛ lawale la w'a tɔgɔ tun te tuma caman masa kɔrɔw fɛ.
eng_text: Interestingly, he was not considered to be very important in ancient times and was not recorded on most ancient king lists.

text: Nka a kaburu yeli san 1922 y'a kɛ tɔgɔtigi ye. Tuma minna kaburu cama wɔgɔbɛra,  se ma kɛ ni kaburu in ma.
eng_text: However, the discovery of his tomb in 1922 made him a celebrity. While many tombs of the past were robbed, this tomb was left virtually undisturbed.

text: Minɛw fanba minnuw su dona Tutankhamun fɛ  tora u cogo la, fɛnɲuman  dilanenw nɛgɛw ni cɛnindenw la be u cɛ la.
eng_text: Most of the items buried with Tutankhamun have been well preserved, including thousands of artefacts made from precious metals and rare stones.

text: Wotorosen kalamanw dilanni ye Asiriyani wotorow fɛgɛya k'u teliya wa k'u labɛn walasa ka kɛlɛkɛcɛw ni wotoro wɛrɛw dan
eng_text: The invention of spoke wheels made Assyrian chariots lighter, faster, and better prepared to outrun soldiers and other chariots.

text: Uka kalaw kisɛw tun be se ka kɛlɛfadenw ka kɛlɛkɛfiniw sɔgɔ. San 1000 yani Yesu bangeli cɛ Asariyaniw ye sokankɛlɛ daminɛ.
eng_text: Arrows from their deadly crossbows could penetrate the armor of rival soldiers. About 1000 B.C., the Assyrians introduced the first cavalry.

text: Sokankɛlɛkɛla ye kɛlɛbolo ye min be kɛlɛ kɛ k'a to so kan. kɛrɛkɛ tun ma dilan fɔlɔ, o la Asariyaniw tun be kɛlɛ kɛ k'u to uka so kɔ jalanw kan.
eng_text: A cavalry is an army that fights on horseback. The saddle had not yet been invented, so the Assyrian cavalry fought on the bare backs of their horses.

text: An be Gɛrɛki politiki mɔgɔ, dɔnnikɛla ni seko ni dɔnko mɔgɔ  caman dɔn,  Holmer de kakan ka kɛ u bɛɛ la tɔgɔtigi ye, ni fiyɛntɔ poyi bɔla dagabana  in, min ye dagabana sɛbɛnni fila kɛ Gɛrɛki sɛbɛnniw la : Iliad ni Odyssey poyiw.
eng_text: We know many Greek politicians, scientists, and artists. Possibly the most known person of this culture is Homer, the legendary blind poet, who composed two masterpieces of Greek literature: the poems Iliad and Odyssey.

text: Sophocoles ni Aristophanes ye hali sisan sɛbɛnnikɛla tɔgɔtigiw ye wa uka sɛbɛnniw be jate diyɛn sɛbɛnni baara baw cɛ la.
eng_text: Sophocles and Aristophanes are still popular playwrights and their plays are considered to be among the greatest works of world literature.

text: Gɛrɛki Jatekalanba tɔgɔtigi dɔ wɛrɛ Pythagoras, min dɔnna kɔsɛbɛ aka kumayira dɔnnen ba in fɛ min be kɛrɛsaba dakɛnyɛlen fanw ni ɲɔgɔn cɛ kan.
eng_text: Another famous Greek is a mathematician Pythagoras, mostly known for his famous theorem about relations of the sides of right triangles.

text: Jate kelen te Hindi kan fɔbaaw hakɛ la. A jatelen do inafɔ kanw bɛɛ la fɔlen filanan k'a se naaninan ma diyɛn kɔnɔ.
eng_text: There are varying estimates for how many people speak Hindi. It is estimated to be between the second and fourth most commonly spoken language in the world.

text: A fakanfɔbaaw hakɛ be yɛlɛma ka tali kɛ ni kan ta cogo jatela walima n'a ma jate.
eng_text: The number of native speakers varies depending on whether or not very closely related dialects are counted.

text: Jateminɛw be munumunu fɔba miliyɔn 340 k'a se miliyɔn 500 ma, wa inafɔ mɔgɔ miliyɔn 800 be se ka kan in faamu.
eng_text: Estimates range from 340 million to 500 million speakers, and as many as 800 million people can understand the language.

text: Hindi kan ni Urudu kan daɲɛw ye kelen ye nka u sɛbɛncogo te kelen ye don o don kumaw la, kan in fila fɔbaw be se ka ɲɔgɔn faamu.
eng_text: Hindi and Urdu are similar in vocabulary but different in script; in everyday conversations, speakers of both languages can usually understand each other.

text: San kɛmɛ sigiyɔrɔma 15na yɔrɔw la, worodugu Ɛsitoni tun be Alimaɲi seko ni dɔnko taabolo la kɔsɛbɛ.
eng_text: Around the 15th century, northern Estonia was under great cultural influence of Germany.

text: Alimaɲikaw ka batokɛla dɔw tun be fɛ  ka Ala surunya  mɔgɔw la, ola u ye Ɛsitoni kan gɛrɛgɛrɛ in dilan.
eng_text: Some German monks wanted to bring God closer to the native people, so they invented the Estonian literal language.

text: A tun b'a sinsin Alimaɲi kan siginidenw kan wa siginiden dɔ "Õ/õ" farala a kan.
eng_text: It was based on the German alphabet and one character "Õ/õ" was added.

text: Ni waati tɛmɛli ye, kanɲɛ caman minnuw singala Alimaɲi kan fɛ ɲagamin'a la. O kɛra Yeelen waati daminɛ ye
eng_text: As time passed, many words that were borrowed from German coalesced. This was the beginning of enlightenment.

text: Laada la, fanga tiyɛntala in tun kakan ka tilen ka taa kɛlɛbolo la a ka kalan kɔfɛ.
eng_text: Traditionally, the heir to the throne would go straight into the military after finishing school.

text: Nka Charles taara sanfɛ kalanso la Trinity Sanfɛ kalanso la, Cambridge yɔrɔ minna a ye Antoropolozi, Arikeyolozi kalan o kɔfɛ Tariku ni 2:2 sɔrɔli ye (duguma kalanso filanan kunnawolosɛbɛn dɔ)
eng_text: However, Charles went to university at Trinity College, Cambridge where he studied Anthropology and Archaeology, and later History, earning a 2:2 (a lower second class degree).

text: Charles tun ye Biritaniki Masa Bɔnda mɔgɔ fɔlɔfɔlɔ ye ka kunnawolosɛbɛn dɔ sɔrɔ.
eng_text: Charles was the first member of the British Royal Family to be awarded a degree.

text: Nasarala Tiriki (Tirasi kɔrɔ walima Urumeli Baliki jikunna) ye jamana 3% ye.
eng_text: European Turkey (eastern Thrace or Rumelia in the Balkan peninsula) includes 3% of the country.

text: Tiriki dugukolo bɛ tɛmɛ kilomɛtɛrɛ 1.600 (nɔngɔn ɲɛ 1.000) kan janyan na ani kilomɛtɛrɛ 800 (nɔngɔn ɲɛ 500) kan boɲan na, ni selekenaani gɔlɔnni ye.
eng_text: The territory of Turkey is more than 1,600 kilometres (1,000 mi) long and 800 km (500 mi) wide, with a roughly rectangular shape.

text: Tiriki dugukolo, k'a fara dalaw kan, bɛ kilomɛtɛrɛ_kare 783.562 (nɔgɔn_kare ɲɛ 300.948) ta, min cɛma kilomɛtɛrɛ_kare 755.688 (nɔngɔn_kare ɲɛ 291.773) Azi worodugu_tilebinyanfan fɛ.
eng_text: Turkey's area, including lakes, occupies 783,562 square kilometres (300,948 sq mi), of which 755,688 square kilometres (291,773 sq mi) are in south west Asia and 23,764 square kilometres (9,174 sq mi) in Europe.

text: Tiriki dugukolo y'a kɛ a ye jamana 37 na ye min ka bon ni diɲɛ jamanaw bɛɛ ye, ani a bɛ ɲini ka Firansi ni Angiletɛri farani ɲɔgɔn kan boɲa bɔ.
eng_text: Turkey's area makes it the world's 37th-largest country, and is about the size of Metropolitan France and the United Kingdom combined.

text: Tiriki kɛrɛ saba lamununa ni kɔgɔji ye: Kɔgɔji Eze tilebin fɛ, Kɔgɔjinfin kɔgɔdugu fɛ ni Kɔgɔji Mediteranɛn worodugu fɛ.
eng_text: Turkey is encircled by seas on three sides: the Aegean Sea to the west, the Black Sea to the north and the Mediterranean Sea to the south.

text: Luxembourg bɔra yɔrɔ jan nka a y'a yɛrɛ ta san 1839.
eng_text: Luxembourg has a long history but its independence dates from 1839.

text: Bɛliziki bi-sigiyɔrɔw tun yed Luxembourg fan dɔ ye fɔlɔ nka u kɛra Bɛliziki ta ye Bɛlizikikaw ka yɛlɛma kɔfɛ san 1830 kɔnɔ.
eng_text: Present-day parts of Belgium were part of Luxembourg in the past but became Belgian after the 1830s Belgian Revolution.

text: Luxembourg y'a ɲini waati bɛɛ la ka to a ka fasabaliya kɔnɔ nka a tun minɛ na Alimakɛlɛfɔlɔ ni filana na Alimaɲi fɛ.
eng_text: Luxembourg has always tried to remain a neutral country but it was occupied in both World War I and World War II by Germany.

text: San 1957 Luxembourg kɛra jɛkulu sigibaga dɔ ye min kodɔnna bi ni Ɛrɔpu Tɔn ye.
eng_text: In 1957 Luxembourg became a founding member of the organization which is today known as the European Union.

text: Drukgyal Dzong ye tarakogo ni Budawdelikɛyɔrɔ ye Paro faaba kɔnɔ (Phondey dugu kɔnɔ).
eng_text: The Drukgyal Dzong is a ruined fortress and Buddhist monastery in the upper part of the Paro District (in Phondey Village).

text: A fɔra ko san 1649, Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel ye taracogo jɔ ka hakilijigi kɛ ka ɲɛsin a ka se ma Tibɛti-Mɔngɔlikaw ka kɛlɛcɛw kan.
eng_text: It is said that in 1649, Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel created the fortress to commemorate his victory against the Tibetan-Mongol forces.

text: San 1951, tasuma dɔ mɛnɛni kɛra sababu ye Drukgyal Dzong jasɛbɛnfura damadama dɔrɔn tora, i n'a fɔ Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal ja.
eng_text: In 1951, a fire caused for only some of the relics of the Drukgyal Dzong to remain, such as the image of Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal.

text: Tasuma banni kɔ, tarakogo marala ni k'a lakana walasa a ka kɛ Bhutan ninkansaramayaw yɔrɔ dɔ ye.
eng_text: After the fire, the fortress was preserved and protected, remaining to be one of Bhutan's most sensational attractions.

text: Kɛmɛsi 18na la Kanbɔji y'a yɛrɛ mɔsɔni sɔrɔ sigiɲɔgɔn setigijamana fila ni ɲɔgɔn cɛ, Tayilandi ni Viyetinamu.
eng_text: During the 18th century Cambodia found itself squeezed between two powerful neighbors, Thailand and Vietnam.

text: Tayilandikaw ye Kanbɔji minɛ siɲɛ caman kɛmɛsi 18na la ani san 1772 u ye Phnom Phen.
eng_text: The Thais invaded Cambodia several times in the 18th century and in 1772 they destroyed Phnom Phen.

text: Kɛmɛsi 18na labanw na Viyetinamukaw fɛnɛ ye Kanbɔji minɛ.
eng_text: In the last years of the 18th century the Vietnamese also invaded Cambodia.

text: Kɛmɛsarada Venezuwelaka 18 tɛ baara la, minnu bɛ baara la u tilankɛ bɛ wari ɲini sira nɔgɔni kan.
eng_text: Eighteen percent of Venezuelans are unemployed, and most of those who are employed work in the informal economy.

text: Venezuwelaka mɔgɔ sabasabasaraw minnu bɛ baara la, fila b'a kɛ forobacakɛda la, naani masuruɲa bɛ baara kɛ bayɛlɛmacakɛda la ani duuru masuruɲa bɛ baara kɛ  sɛnɛda la.
eng_text: Two thirds of Venezuelans who work do so in the service sector, nearly a quarter work in industry and a fifth work in agriculture.

text: Venezuwelakaw fɛ bayɛlɛmacakɛda nafama dɔ ye taji ye, minna jamana ye kɔkanfeerekɛraba ye, hali n'a sɔrɔ kɛmɛsarada kelen dɔrɔn de bɛ baara kɛ tajibayɛlɛmacakɛda la.
eng_text: An important industry for Venezuelans is oil, where the country is a net exporter, even though only one percent work in the oil industry.

text: Ka kɔn jamana ka yɛrɛta ɲɛ, Sɛngapuri Yirifalenyɔrɔkodɔnnaw ye dɛmɛ kɛ ka gun yɛlɛma ka kɛ duguYirifalenyɔrɔsumamanba ye.
eng_text: Early in the nation's independence, Singapore Botanic Gardens' expertise helped to transform the island into a tropical Garden City.

text: San 1981, Vanda Miss Joaquim, feerewoloso dɔ min tara ka kɛ jamana feere ye.
eng_text: In 1981, Vanda Miss Joaquim, an orchid hybrid, was chosen as the nation's national flower.

text: San o san Ɔtɔburu waati a ka surun bindunbaganw miliyɔn 1,5 minnu bɛ yaala ka taa worodugu lɛw kuntilenna na, ni ka Ba Mara tigɛ, kaɲɛkana kuluw fan fɛ san nɔfɛ.
eng_text: Every year around October nearly 1.5 million herbivores travel towards the southern plains, crossing the Mara River, from the northern hills for the rains.

text: O kɔ u bɛ baani na tilebin fɛ, ka Ba Mara tigɛ tugunni, sanw kɔfɛ Avirili waati.
eng_text: And then back to the north through the west, once again crossing the Mara river, after the rains in around April.

text: Serengeti forobakungobagawmarayɔrɔ, Ngorongoro fɛnkɔrɔwmarayɔrɔ ni Maswa Tolonkɛnɛ Tanzani kɔnɔ ani Maasai ForobaKɛnɛkɛrɛnkɛrɛnni Kɛniya kɔnɔ bɛ Serengeti mara kɔnɔ.
eng_text: The Serengeti region contains the Serengeti National Park, the Ngorongoro Conservation Area and Maswa Game Reserve in Tanzania and the Maasai Mara National Reserve in Kenya.

text: Kumaɲɔgɔnyasiraw dilannikalan mako bɛ bɛnkan-ni -kɔrɔnidɔnniw la, ka fara baarakɛminandɔnniw la kumaɲɔgɔnyakalanw na (fɛnkɔrɔmara, kumakan ni jadilan, tarikulakale ani caman wɛrɛw.)
eng_text: Learning to create interactive media requires conventional and traditional skills, as well as tools mastered in interactive classes (storyboarding, audio and video editing, story telling, etc.)

text: Kumaɲɔgɔnyaɲɛgɛn mako bɛ i k'i hakilinaw jateminɛ tugun kumalase kan ani i ka miiri kalan sira caman kan.
eng_text: Interactive design requires that you re-assess your assumptions about media production and learn to think in a non-linear ways.

text: Kumaɲɔgɔnyaja mako b'a la ko porozɛkɔnɔfɛnw ka tugu ɲɔgɔnna, nka fɛnɛ u kelenkelenna ka baara kɛ.
eng_text: Interactive design requires that components of a project connect to each other, but also make sense as a separate entity.

text: Zooms kɔlɔ ye fokali gƐlƐya ni kuntilenna fƐn minw hakƐka kan yasa fokaliw cƐjanɲa gamu sɔrɔ kaɲi kɔsɔbƐ ka tƐmƐ kuntilenna folow kan.
eng_text: The disadvantage of zoom lenses is that the focal complexity and number of lens elements required to achieve a range of focal lengths is much greater than for prime lenses.

text: Dɔ be bɔ gƐlƐya in na ni lentiye dilanbaw ye  lantiye dilan hakƐ dɔw sɔrɔ minw ka ca kɔsɔbƐ
eng_text: This is becoming less of an issue as lens manufacturers achieve higher standards in lens production.

text: Nin de ye a to zoom be se ka jaa dɔw bɔ min suguya be kaɲa ni suguya ye min sɔrɔla ni fokali janɲa kuntilenɲa ye.
eng_text: This has allowed zoom lenses to produce pictures of a quality comparable to that achieved by lenses with fixed focal length.

text: Zoom kuntilenɲa kɔlɔ wɛrɛ ye ko kuntilenɲa dayɛlɛnnen ba ( Teliya) ka fɛgɛn kɔsɔbɛ tuma cama.
eng_text: Another disadvantage of zoom lenses is that the maximum aperture (the speed) of the lens is usually lower.

text: O be a to zumew da dumanw be labarali be gƐlƐya yeelen fƐgƐman  lahalayaw la min ni felasi tƐ ala.
eng_text: This makes inexpensive zoom lenses hard to use in low-light conditions without a flash.

text: Thĩna ũrĩa mũnene hĩndi ya kũgeria gũcenjia thenema  ĩtuĩke DVD nĩ overscan.
eng_text: One of the most common problems when trying to convert a movie to DVD format is the overscan.

text: TV nyingĩ cithondeketwo nĩguo cikenie mũingĩ.
eng_text: Most televisions are made in a way to please the general public.

text: Gwa gĩtũmi kĩu, kĩndũ kĩrĩa gĩothe wonaga TV inĩ kĩarĩ na mĩhaka ĩtinitio igũrũ, thĩ na mĩena.
eng_text: For that reason, everything you see on the TV had the borders cut, top, bottom and sides.

text: ũndũ ũyũ wĩkagwo nĩguo mbica iihũre gĩcicioinĩ gĩothe. ũndu ũyũ witagwo overscan.
eng_text: This is made to ensure that the image covers the whole screen. That is called overscan.

text: Kwa mutino, ungĩthondeka DVD, kwĩna uhoteku ĩtinio mĩicoinĩ, na angĩkorwo thenema nĩ irarĩ na tũcunjĩ tũkuhĩrĩirie thi, tutikuonanio tuothe.
eng_text: Unfortunately, when you make a DVD, it's borders will most likely be cut too, and if the video had subtitles too close to the bottom, they won't be fully shown.

text: Mĩako ya tene ya nyũmba cia athamaki nĩikoretwo ĩcũngĩrĩirie meciria na kũrehe mbica cia haro mecirianĩ na cia mbarathi cia Arthur.
eng_text: The traditional medieval castle has long inspired the imagination, conjuring up images of jousts, banquets and Arthurian chivalry.

text: Ona ĩrũgamĩtio gatagatĩ ka matigari ma mĩako ya mĩaka ngiri ĩmwe nĩ ũhũthũ kũririkana mĩgambo na mĩnungo ya mbara thiru, hakuhĩ kũigua makinya ma mbarathi igũrũ rĩa mĩaro ya mahiga na kũigua mũnungo wa guoya ũkiuma marima ma kũiga ohũo.
eng_text: Even standing amidst thousand year-old ruins it is easy to bring to mind the sounds and smells of battles long gone, to almost hear the clatter of hooves on the cobbles and to smell the fear rising from the dungeon pits.

text: No mwĩcirĩrie witũ nĩũrugamĩtio na ma? Nyũmba nene cia athamaki ciakagwo nĩkĩ? Ciacorirwo na cigĩakwo atĩa?
eng_text: But is our imagination based on reality? Why were castles built in the first place? How were they designed and built?

text: Faamaso Kirby Muxloe tun ye tata ye ka tɛmɛ faamaso yɛrɛ kan, min tun ye o waatibaaranɔn  ye.
eng_text: Typical for the period, Kirby Muxloe Castle is more of a fortified house than a true castle.

text: A ka filantɛrɛnɔrɔlenbaw ni kogopɛnpɛrɛnlenw ye waatijankɛlɛbuniw kun.
eng_text: Its large glazed windows and thin walls would not have been able to resist a determined attack for long.

text: 1480 sanw kɔnɔ, a jɔli daminɛlen Lord Hastings fɛ, kayira tun bɛ jamana fanbɛ la ani lakana tun bɛ ɲini fo ni coolokuluni dɔw tun nana binkani na.
eng_text: In the 1480s, when its construction was begun by Lord Hastings, the country was relatively peaceful and defense was only required against small bands of roving marauders.

text: Fangalatilen tun ye taabolo dɔ ye minna Erɔpu jamanaw tun bɛ a ɲinina  ka Erɔpu jamanaw bɛɛ ka taya makaran.
eng_text: The balance of power was a system in which European nations sought to maintain the national sovereignty of all European states.

text: Hakilina tun ye ko Erɔpu jamanaw bɛɛ ka a ɲini ka jamana kelen bali ka fangaba sɔrɔ, o la jamanamarabulonw tun bɛ u ka jɛɲɔgɔnyaw yɛlɛmayɛlɛma waati dɔ la walasa ka fanga tilenlen to.
eng_text: The concept was that all European nations had to seek to prevent one nation from becoming powerful, and thus national governments often changed their alliances in order to maintain the balance.

text: Ɛsipaɲi fanga yɛlɛmayɛlɛma kɛlɛ ye kɛlɛ fɔlɔdaminɛ yira min jujɔn tun ye fangalatilen ye.
eng_text: The War of Spanish Succession marked the first war whose central issue was the balance of power.

text: O kɛra yɛlɛmaba dɔ taamasiɲɛ ye, komi Ɛrɔpu jamanaw tun tɛ na u yɛrɛ bila diinɛkokɛlɛw la tun. O la sa, San Bisabakɛlɛ kɛra diinɛkɛlɛ dɔ taamasiɲɛ ye.
eng_text: This marked an important change, as European powers would no longer have the pretext of being religious wars. Thus, the Thirty Years' War would be the last war to be labeled a religious war.

text: Artemis sɔnnikɛyɔrɔ Ephesus tun cɛnna zuwekalo tile 21, san 356 ka kɔn Yesu bangeli ɲɛ tasumadonwale ye Herostratus fɛ.
eng_text: The temple of Artemis at Ephesus was destroyed on July 21, 356 BCE in an act of arson committed by Herostratus.

text: Tariku kɔnɔ, a ka cɛsiri tun ye a tɔgɔ bɔ cogo bɛɛ la. Ephesuskaw ye nɛnini kɛ, ni ka fɔ ko Herostratus tɔgɔ kanna lase bele.
eng_text: According to the story, his motivation was fame at any cost. The Ephesians, outraged, announced that Herostratus' name never be recorded.

text: Girɛsi kokɔrɔwɲɛɲinibaga Strabo y'a tɔgɔ sɛbɛn, i n'a fɔ anw y'a dɔn cogo minna bi.Sɔnnikɛyɔrɔ cɛnna don min su Zulu Kara Nani bangera.
eng_text: The Greek historian Strabo later noted the name, which is how we know today. The temple was destroyed on the same night that Alexander the Great was born.

text: Zulu Kara Nani, k'a to masaya la, y'a ɲini ka mɔgɔw sara ka sɔnnikɛyɔrɔ in kurakuraya, ɲa ban kɛra a ka laɲini ma. kɔfɛ, Zulu Kara Nani saalen kɔ, sɔnnikɛyɔrɔ kurakurayara san 323 Yesu Bangelen kɔ.
eng_text: Alexander, as king, offered to pay to rebuild the temple, but his offer was denied. Later, after Alexander died, the temple was rebuilt in 323 BCE.

text: A dɔn ka a fɔ ko i tɛgɛ labilalen do kosɛbɛ i kɛ tɔ ka fɔlikanw bɛɛ fɔ koɲuma - ani fɛnɛ a lajɛ i ka na yɛlɛmakura caman kɛ ni i bolodennkɔniw ye.
eng_text: Make sure your hand is as relaxed as possible while still hitting all the notes correctly - also try not to make much extraneous motion with your fingers.

text: O cogo la, i bɛna i yɛrɛ sɛgɛn dɔɔnindɔɔnin. N hakili lajigi ko nafa tɛ a la ka kilew gosi ni fangaba ye mankanba nɔfɛ i n'a fɔ piyano kan.
eng_text: This way, you will tire yourself out as little as possible. Remember there's no need to hit the keys with a lot of force for extra volume like on the piano.

text: Akɔridiyɔn kan, walasa ka mankan layɛlɛ, i bɛ nɛgɛniw digi ni fanga ni teliya dɔɔnin ye.
eng_text: On the accordion, to get extra volume, you use the bellows with more pressure or speed.

text: Misitisisimi ye nɔnnabɔ ye ka ɲɛsin  diinɛkulu ma, farafasiyali ma, walema tiɲɛnlaban,-alakosuma,-diinɛtiɲɛn,-walema alakowajuliŋuma ma.
eng_text: Mysticism is the pursuit of communion with, identity with, or conscious awareness of an ultimate reality, divinity, spiritual truth, or God.

text: Danaba bɛ dɔnnitilennni, hakilina, walema  dinɛkosɛgɛsɛgɛli/alakosɛgɛsɛgɛli walema jowsɛgɛsɛgɛli ɲɛɲini.
eng_text: The believer seeks a direct experience, intuition, or insight into divine reality/the deity or dieties.

text: Mantow bɛ taabolo walema kɛwale dɔw ta minnu kun ye ka o dɔnniw lakunu.
eng_text: Followers pursue certain ways of living, or practices that are intended to nurture those experiences.

text: Misitisisimi bɛ danfara ka bɔ diinɛ tɔ wɛrɛw ka danaya ni baato la ni a ka sinsinni ye mɔgɔ ka hakilinatigɛ dɔrɔn ye, kɛrɛnkɛrɛnyala minnu bɛ bɛn, jateminɛba, nusɔndiya, walema sewa kunkan.
eng_text: Mysticism can be distinguished from other forms of religious belief and worship by its emphasis on the direct personal experience of a unique state of consciousness, particularly those of a peaceful, insightful, blissful, or even ecstatic character.

text: Sikhism ye diinɛ ye ka bɔ Ɛndi danguni na. A bɔra Punjab mara la kɛmɛsi 15na waati ka bɔ kabila bolofara dɔ ka diinɛ bolofara dɔ la Hindu laada kɔnɔ.
eng_text: Sikhism is a religion from the Indian sub-continent. It originated in the Punjab region during the 15th century from a sectarian split within the Hindu tradition.

text: Sikhs bɛ u ka diinɛ danfara ka bɔ Hinduyisimi na ka diinɛ dannan hali ni a sɔrɔ u bɛ a dɔn ko a ju ni a laadaw bɔra Hinduyisimi na.
eng_text: Sikhs consider their faith to be a separate religion from Hinduism though they acknowledge its Hindu roots and traditions.

text: Sikhs bɛ a fɔ u ka diinɛ ma ko Gurmat, min ye Punjabi ye "guru taabolo kan". Guru ye Ɛndi diinɛw bɛɛ sinsinbeereba ye guru ye nka Sikhism na a ye nafan dɔ sɔrɔ min bɛ kɛ Sikhs ka danayabakuruba ye.
eng_text: Sikhs call their religion Gurmat, which is Punjabi for "way of the guru". The guru is a fundamental aspect of all Indian religions but in Sikhism has taken on an importance that forms the core of Sikh beliefs.

text: Diinɛ in bangera kɛmɛsi 15nan na Guru Nanak fɛ (1469-1539). Guru 9 wɛrɛw ye ɲɔgɔn falen.
eng_text: The religion was founded in the 15th century by Guru Nanak (1469–1539). There followed in succession a further nine gurus.

text: O n'a bɛɛ Zuyekalo la san 1956, Kruschev ka lahiduw gɛlɛyara k'a sabu kɛ Pɔlɔɲi mankanw min senfɛ baarakɛlaw murutila balokodɛsɛ ni sara jiginni na, k'a laban foroba murutili la Kominizimu kama.
eng_text: However, in June 1956, Krushchev's promises were put to the test when riots in Poland, where workers were protesting against food shortages and wage cuts, turned into a general protest against Communism.

text: Hali ni labanna Kruschev ye mugucimɔbili bila ka ta basigilanati, a dɛsɛra sɔrɔsira gɛlɛya dɔw la an'a sɔnna ka jamatigi Wadyslaw Gomulka kɛ Minisiri Ɲɛmɔgɔ kura ye.
eng_text: Although in the end, Krushchev sent in tanks to restore order, he did give way to some economic demands and agreed to appoint the popular Wladyslaw Gomulka as the new prime minister.

text: Indus ka kurukanfolon tabiya tun ye Nsiranɛgɛ Tile tabiya ye Ɛndi kaɲɛka-tibinyanfan bangudeni la min ye bi  Pakistan ni Ɛndi kaɲɛka-tilebinmaraw dɔ ye ani Afiganisitan kaɲɛka-kɔrɔnyanfan lamini.
eng_text: The Indus Valley Civilization was a Bronze Age civilisation in the northwest Indian subcontinent encompassing most of modern-day Pakistan and some regions in northwest India and northeast Afghanistan.

text: Tabiya in yiriwala Indus  Badaw la min y'a tɔgɔ di a ma.
eng_text: The civilisation flourished in the basins of the Indus River wherefore it derives its name.

text: Hali n'a y'a sɔrɔ kodɔnna dɔw be k'a ŋunuŋunu ko k'a d'a kan ko tabiya  in fana tunbe sisan  Sarasvati badingɛw la, n'o jara bi, a tɔgɔ tun kakan ka kɛ Indus-Sarasvati tabiya ye k'a sɔrɔ dɔw b'a fɔ a ma Harappan tabiya,  Harappa bolo aka yɔrɔw fɔlɔfɔlɔw min wɔgɔbɛra 1920 sanw na.
eng_text: Although some scholars speculate that since the civilisation also existed in the basins of the now dried up Sarasvati River, it should be aptly called the Indus-Sarasvati Civilization, while some call it the Harappan Civilization after Harappa, the first of its sites to be excavated in the 1920s.

text: Roman Fangamara kɛlɛhakilina sira y'u dɛmɛ ka furakɛli ɲɛtaaw sɔrɔ.
eng_text: The militaristic nature of the Roman empire aided in the development of medical advances.

text: Furakɛlikɛlalaw y'a daminɛ ka ta baara la Fangamasa Augustus fɛ wa u ye Roman Furakɛlikɛli Baarakɛbolo fɔlɔ sigi senkan min tun kakan ka baarakɛ kɛlɛ kɔfɛ.
eng_text: Doctors began to be recruited by Emperor Augustus and even formed the first Roman Medical Corps for use in the aftermath of battles.

text: Farali furakɛlikɛlalaw ye dimidalafura caman dɔn inafɔ mɔrifini k'a bɔ sayiyirini kisɛw la ani isicopolamini k'a bɔ fogofogoyiri kisɛw la.
eng_text: Surgeons had knowledge of various sedatives including morphine from extracts of poppy seeds and scopolamine from herbane seeds.

text: U jola tigɛli sira fɛ walasa ka banabaatɔw kisi kɛlɛbɛ ma ani sirili ni jolisiraw digili ye walasa ka joli munumunu kunbɛ.
eng_text: They became proficient at amputation to save patients from gangrene as well as tourniquets and arterial clamps to stem blood flow.

text: Sankɛmɛsigi caman na Roman Fangamara kɛra sabu ye ka ɲɛtaa ba caman sɔrɔ furakɛli sira fɛ ani ka dɔnni fanba labɛn an be min dɔn bi.
eng_text: Over multiple centuries, the Roman empire led to great gains in the field of medicine and formed much of the knowledge we know today.

text: Purelans origami ye origami dɔ ye minna kuriko kelen dɔrɔn de be se ka kɛ waati kelen kɔnɔ, kuruli gɛlɛnmanw ma daga inafɔ kuruli wolokilen, wa yɔrɔ ɲɔgɔnmanw de be kuruliw bɛɛ la.
eng_text: Pureland origami is origami with the restriction that only one fold may be done at a time, more complex folds like reverse folds are not allowed, and all folds have straightforward locations.

text: A tun labɛnna John Smith fɛ san 1970w kɔnɔna na walasa ka kurulikɛla kuraw dɛmɛ walima minnu lujuralen do.
eng_text: It was developed by John Smith in the 1970s to help inexperienced folders or those with limited motor skills.

text: Denmisɛniw be bɔ siyako ani siyako kɔlɔlɔw kalama denmisɛniya kɔnɔ ani o siyako kɔlɔlɔ be ziye o ka tagabolo kan.
eng_text: Children develop an awareness of race and racial stereotypes quite young and these racial stereotypes affect behavior.

text: Misalila, denmisɛniw minunw b'o yɛrɛ jati siyakulu fitini dɔ fɔ min kofɔlen ka baara kɛ ekɔlila tɛ baara kɛ ekolila tumamina nin u bɔra nin kuma in kalaman min tugulen u ka siyala.
eng_text: For instance, children who identify with a racial minority that is stereotyped as not doing well in school tend to not do well in school once they learn about the stereotype associated with their race.

text: Rũrenda rũrĩa rwa gatatũ kũmenyekana mũno nĩ ta MySpace bũrũri-inĩ wa Amerika, na rũtũmagĩro nĩ arũmĩrĩri matanyihĩirie millioni mĩrongo ĩtano na inya.
eng_text: MySpace is the third most popular website used in the United States and has 54 million profiles currently.

text: Ngenda ta icio nĩ irarũmbũyanio nacio mũno, na makiria ciikaro inĩ cia mathomo.
eng_text: These websites have gotten a lot of attention, especially in the education setting.

text: Kwĩna maũndũ mega metanĩtio na rũrenda, ta guthondeka irathi mĩtamboini kũrĩa mathomo maraheano na njĩra cia mbica, video,  maandĩko na mangĩ ta macio.
eng_text: There are positive aspects to these websites, which include, being able to easily setup a class page which can include blogs, videos, photos, and other features.

text: Page ĩno no ĩkinyĩrĩke na ihenya na njĩra ya kũheana rũrenda o rũmwe, ũndu ũrĩa ũhotithagia kũririkana kwa na ihenya, na gũteithia arutwo arĩa mena thĩna wa gũtũmira keyboard kana gũthondeka maritwa.
eng_text: This page can easily be accessed by providing just one web address, which makes it easy to remember and easy to type in for students who may have trouble using the keyboard or with spelling.

text: No ĩthondeko nĩguo ĩhũthie mathomo, na cĩĩkĩro marangi na kũringana na wendi wa ene.
eng_text: It can be customized to make it easy to read and also with as much or little color as desired.

text: "Jatekɛminɛbaliya Bana" ye nzɛbɛn bana ye min be ɲɛfɔ kɔrɔlen nin bana saba ye, nin o ye balikakokɛ ye, tulonkɛ ani boliboli damatɛmɛ walima "kisɛya damatɛmɛlen".
eng_text: Attention Deficit Disorder "is a neurological syndrome whose classic defining triad of symptoms including impulsivity, distractibility, and hyperactivity or excess energy".

text: O tɛ kalan lujura ye, o ye kalanli ɲakamu ye; a be se "mɔgɔ 3 ka ta 5 la denmisɛniw la, lala mɔgɔɔ cama inafɔ Amerikɛn denmisɛni miliyɔn 2".
eng_text: It is not a learning disability, it is a learning disorder; it "affects 3 to 5 percent of all children, perhaps as many as 2 million American children".

text: Jatekɛminɛbaliya Bana be denmisɛni minunw na be gɛlɛya sɔrɔ walasa ko ɲɛsin fɛnw ma inafɔ lɛkɔli baara, nka u be seka ɲsɛin fɛnw ma minw ka d'o ye inafɔ zuye kɛli walima i jaɲɛ wakulɔni filɛli walima kumasen sɛbɛni nin tomi sɛbɛn baliya ye.
eng_text: Children with ADD have a hard time focusing on things like school work, but they can concentrate on things they enjoy doing like playing games or watching their favorite cartoons or writing sentences without punctuation.

text: U denmisɛniw b'u yɛrɛ do kunbalan cama na bari u be dɔn "farati kow la, kɛlɛw la, fagan sɔsɔ baaraw la" walasa ka hakili nisondiya ba bari u hakili tɛ nisondiya nin fɛɛrɛ nɔrɔmaliw ye.
eng_text: These children tend to get into a lot of trouble, because they "engage in risky behaviors, get into fights, and challenge authority" in order to stimulate their brain, since their brain can not be stimulated by normal methods.

text: Jatekɛminɛbaliya Bana be dangari mɔgɔyala nin u tɔɲɔgɔn ye bari denmisɛni tɔw tɛ sek'a famuya kun mina u be kewale kɛ u be minunw kɛ walima muna u be kalanikɛ u b'a kɛ cogomina walima u ka mɔgɔbayara cogo nin tɔ ta tɛ kelen ye.
eng_text: ADD affects relationships with other peers because other children can not understand why they act the way that they do or why they spell they way they do or that their maturity level is different.

text: Komi dɔni sɔrɔli ani kalanli se yɛlɛmala cogola inafɔ a fɔra sanfɛ cogomina, o jateminɛ nɔrɔmali mina dɔni be sɔrɔ yɛlɛmala.
eng_text: As the ability to obtain knowledge and to learn changed in such a way as mentioned above the base rate at which knowledge was obtained changed.

text: Fɛɛrɛ walasa ka kunafoni sɔrɔ n'o tɛ kelen ye. Piresiyon tɛyi tuguni mɔgɔ kelen ka mirila, nka mirili gafe la se kɛra piriyorite  ba ye.
eng_text: The approach to obtaining information was different. No longer did pressure reside within individual recall, but the ability to recall text became more of a focus.

text: Duguma jateminɛla, Renaissance ye yɛlɛma ba dɔn kalanli fɛɛrɛ la ani dɔni carilila.
eng_text: In essence, the Renaissance made a significant change in the approach to learning and the dissemination of knowledge.

text: Ka dan bɔ dantanfɛnw tɔw la minunw be ko adamaden,  homodiw t'u tigɛ nati tuguni ka tama walima dɔni ɲun walima ka panpan yiriw ni ɲɔgɔn cɛ.
eng_text: Unlike other primates, hominids no longer use their hands in locomotion or bearing weight or swinging through the trees.

text: Siyenpanzew tigɛ ani sen ka surun boɲan ani jaɲa na, jiralikɛlila tigɛ natilila dɔni ɲunila ka tama tigɛ gunkunkan.
eng_text: The chimpanzee's hand and foot are similar in size and length, reflecting the hand's use for bearing weight in knuckle walking.

text: Adamaden tigɛ ka surun ka tɛmɛ sen kan, nin tigɛgɔnidenw tileni ye.
eng_text: The human hand is shorter than the foot, with straighter phalanges.

text: Sukɔrɔ tigɛkolo, san miliyɔn filia ka se saba ma kɔrɔya, be nin yɛlɛma tigɛ baaraw la jira kabɔ tamala ka ta yɛlɛma yɛlɛmalima.
eng_text: Fossil hand bones two million to three million years old reveal this shift in specialization of the hand from locomotion to manipulation.

text: Mɔgɔ dɔw dalen n'ala ko suko dilanlen jɔlen cama natili be seka sɛgɛ damatɛmɛ wale nati.
eng_text: Some people believe that experiencing many artificially induced lucid dreams often enough can be very exhausting.

text: Nin fenomɛnini kun jɔnjɔn  ye suko jɔlenw jaabi min be waati janya nɛtugu ka dayɛlɛw ni ɲɔgɔn cɛ.
eng_text: The main reason for this phenomenon is the result of the lucid dreams expanding the length of time between REM states.

text: Nin nɛtugu ka dayɛlɛw dama damani ɲɔgɔn cɛ su kɔnɔ, nin cogoya in i be sunɔgɔ kɛ ani i faikolo be yɛrɛ sɔrɔ bɛ dɔgɔya kosɛbɛ f'a be kɛ kunbalan ye.
eng_text: With fewer REMs per night, this state in which you experience actual sleep and your body recovers becomes infrequent enough to become a problem.

text: O sɛgɛ ka jugu inafɔ nin kun be ka wili sanga muganw san muganw walima sanga bisabaw sanga bisabaw ani ka jabarani lajɛ.
eng_text: This is just as exhausting as if you were to wake up every twenty or thirty minutes and watch TV.

text: O kɔlɔlɔ sirileno cogomina ani waatidamina i nzɛbɛn ba ɲinin ka suko jɛlen k'i be bɔ min kalaman.
eng_text: The effect is dependent on how often your brain attempts to lucidly dream per night.

text: Maũndũ matiathire wega kuuma o kĩambĩrĩria kũrĩ Aitariano arĩa maari Rũgongo rwa Afirika. Kahinda ini ka kiumia kĩmwe thutha wa Itari gutangatha mbaara kurĩ mweri wa gatandatũ 10, 1940, mbatu ya Ngeretha ya Hussars 11 niyegwatiire Fort Capuzzo kuu Libya.
eng_text: Things did not go well for the Italians in North Africa almost from the start. Within a week of Italy's declaration of war on June 10, 1940, the British 11th Hussars had seized Fort Capuzzo in Libya.

text: Kuhĩtũkira ihithũkĩra Irathĩro rĩa Bardia, Ngeretha niyanyitire mĩgwate General Lastucci ũrĩa warĩ Inginia mũnene wa mbatũ ya Itari rĩa Ikũmi..
eng_text: In an ambush east of Bardia, the British captured the Italian Tenth Army's Engineer-in-Chief, General Lastucci.

text: Kũrĩ mweri wa gatandatũ 28, Marshal Italo Balbo, ũrĩa warĩ Gavana Mũnene wa Libya na mũgai wa Mussolini nĩoragirwo nĩ mbũtũ ciao o hĩndĩ akinya Tobruk.
eng_text: On June 28, Marshal Italo Balbo, the Governor-General of Libya and apparent heir to Mussolini, was killed by friendly fire while landing in Tobruk.

text: Farikoloɲɛnajɛ kura ɛsikirimu be zuye niwo cama na, ka daminɛ sanfɛ kalandenw la minunw y'a kalan sanfɛ kalansola ka ta bila a dɔn ba nganaw la Olɛnpiki tulɔnkɛla la.
eng_text: The modern sport of fencing is played at many levels, from students learning at a university to professional and Olympic competition.

text: Farikoloɲɛnajɛ in be zuye fɔlɔfɔlɔ ɲɔgɔndan cogoyala, ɛsikirimlu zuyeba kelen ani dɔwɛrɛ.
eng_text: The sport is primarily played in a duel format, one fencer dueling another.

text: Gɔlifu ye farikoloɲɛnɛjɛ je min n'a zuyebaw be jiri fɛrɛn do labaara ka balɔn bugɔ ka dɔn wɔni kɔnɔ.
eng_text: Golf is a game in which players use clubs to hit balls into holes.

text: Zuye fan fɔlɔ be kɛ wɔni tanisegin la, nin zuyekɛraw daminɛli ye waatibɛla wɔni fɔlɔla ani taleɲɛ ba laban wɔni taniseginanla.
eng_text: Eighteen holes are played during a regular round, with players usually starting on the first hole on the course and finishing on the eighteenth.

text: Zuwekɛra min bɔni fitini kɛ, walima jirifɛrɛ yɛlɛma yɛlɛma dafa ka turu sebaya sɔrɔ.
eng_text: The player who takes the fewest strokes, or swings of the club, to complete the course wins.

text: Zuwe be kɛ bin sanfɛ ani bin min be wɔni da gɛrɛfɛ tigɛlen kokɛ fitini ani be wele green.
eng_text: The game is played on grass, and the grass around the hole is mown shorter and called the green.

text: Lala turisimu cogoya carili kodɔnlen ye mɔgɔw be min tugu tamala: tulɔnkɛ yɔrɔlajɛli.
eng_text: Perhaps the most common type of tourism is what most people associate with traveling: Recreation tourism.

text: O ye waatimine nin mɔgɔw tara yɔrɔ dɔ la min no ka dɔngɔndɔ diɲɛlatigɛ tɛ kelen ye walasa ka lafiya ani k'o yɛrɛ ɲɛnɛjɛ.
eng_text: This is when people go to a place that is very different from their regular day-to-day life to relax and have fun.

text: Kɔkɔjidaw, tulɔnkɛyɔrɔ parikiw, ani sigiyɔrɔw de ye yɔrɔ kodɔnlenw ye yɛrɛɲɛba turisiw be ta yɔrɔmina kosɛbɛ.
eng_text: Beaches, theme parks and camp grounds are often the most common places frequented by recreational tourists.

text: Nin mɔgɔ dɔ ka yɔrɔlajɛli kun ye ka ta yɔrɔ kɛrɛnkɛrɛne dɔla walasa ko tariku dɔ ani tabolo, o la o o yɔrɔlajɛ cogo dɔnlen no inafɔ yɔrɔtabolodɔn yɔrɔlajɛ.
eng_text: If the objective of one’s visit to a particular place is to get to know its history and culture then this type of tourism is known as cultural tourism.

text: Turisiw be seka jamana kɛrɛnkɛrɛn dɔ yɔrɔ nafanw cama lajɛ walima u be seka sugandi ka sinsin yɔrɔ kelen dɔrɔn kuna.s
eng_text: Tourists may visit different landmarks of a particular country or they may simply opt to focus on just one area.

text: faganmarakɛlaw, o baara lajɛlila, kun ye laɲinin kɛ sabatilila.
eng_text: The Colonists, seeing this activity, had also called for reinforcements.

text: Kɛlɛkuluw minunw ye nɛfɛ yɔrɔ sabati kun ye New Hampshire kɛlɛbolo 1 ani 2 mɔgɔ 200 ye, kolonɛli John Stark ani Reed ka mara kɔnɔ (u fila bɛɛ kɛla zɛnɛrali ye).
eng_text: Troops reinforcing the forward positions included the 1st and 3rd New Hampshire regiments of 200 men, under Colonels John Stark and James Reed (both later became generals).

text: Stark ka mɔgɔw jɔra dakɔrɔra gɛrɛfɛ kɔkɔdugu yanfan dan na faganmarakɛlaw ka jɔyɔrɔla.
eng_text: Stark's men took positions along the fence on the north end of the Colonist's position.

text: Nin ji funu fitini ye wo dayɛlɛ Mystic Riŋer fanfɛ penɛnsili kɔkɔdugu ni kɔrɔn yanfan fɛ, u ye sinsan bɔɲan jɔna nin kabkuru kɔgɔ surumaniye kɔkɔ yanfan dan fɔ ji dagolola jida fitini sanfɛ.
eng_text: When low tide opened a gap along the Mystic River along the northeast of the peninsula, they quickly extended the fence with a short stone wall to the north ending at the water's edge on a small beach.

text: Gidley walima Start kun ye poto  jɔ piye 100 bɔɲɔgɔngo (mɛtiri 30) sinsan nɛfɛ ani ye ɔridiri di ko mɔgɔsi kana mugu ci fo waatimina nin u yɛrɛw ka kɛlɛkɛdenw tɛmɛna la.

eng_text: Maintaining a healthy energy balance, practicing effective hydration habits, and understanding the various aspects of supplementation practices can help athletes improve their performance and increase their enjoyment of the sport.

eng_text: Products can be purchased as needed, but most will have little or no real impact on performance.

eng_text: Its a very complex entity which consists, according to a simplified Bohr model, of a central nucleus orbited by electrons, somewhat similar to planets orbiting the sun - see Figure 1.1.

eng_text: When all individuals in a population are identical with regard to a particular phenotypic trait they are known as monomorphic.

text: Farikolodenfitini ye mun ye? Farikolodenfitini danɛ bɔra Latin danɛla "cella", min kɔrɔ ye "bɔn fitini", ani a fɔra siyɛnfɔlɔ mikorosikɔpu lajɛli ba dɔ fɛ min be ka jirifara dilan cogo lajɛ.
eng_text: What is a cell? The word cell comes from the Latin word "cella", meaning "small room", and it was first coined by a microscopist observing the structure of cork.

text: Farikolobɔn ye fɛn fitini ye niman fɛnw bɛla, ani farilifanw bɛɛ dilan neno nin farikolobɔn da kelen walima camaw ye.
eng_text: The cell is the basic unit of all living things, and all organisms are composed of one or more cells.

text: Farikolobɔnw ye fɛn fitini ani mako kabɔn ɲɛnɛmaya kalanlila, tiɲɛla, nin u be wele ko "ɲɛnɛmaya sojɔlanw".
eng_text: Cells are so basic and critical to the study of life, in fact, that they are often referred to as "the building blocks of life".

text: Fasajuru sira b'a cogoya mara nin fasa cikanw cilile ka ta farikolola walasa ka joli bolili t'o cogola ani o ciyɛnli.
eng_text: The Nervous System maintains homeostasis by sending nerve impulses through out the body to keep the flow of blood going as well as undisturbed.

text: Nin fasa cikanw be seka ci jɔna jɔna farikolo fɛ min be farikolo lakana kabɔ kɔlɔlɔ dɔ ma.
eng_text: These nerve impulses can be sent so quickly throughout the body which helps keep the body safe from any potential threat.

text: Fiyɛnkolɔɔn be jirijuw bɔn, a be sojanw jirifɛrɛnw ta kabɔ u kuna, ani ka mɔbiliw ta k'u fili sanfɛ. Fiyɛnkolɔn fan juguma fila te tɛmɛ nɛgɛ kanɛ saban kan.
eng_text: Tornadoes strike a small area compared to other violent storms, but they can destroy everything in their path.

eng_text: Tornadoes uproot trees, rip boards from buildings, and fling cars up into the sky. The most violent two percent of tornadoes last more than three hours.

eng_text: Many people dream of the day when humans can travel to another star and explore other worlds, some people wonder what's out there some belive that aliens or other life may live on another plant.

eng_text: But, if this ever does happen probably won't happen for a very long time. The stars are so spread out that there are trillions of miles between stars that are "neighbors".

eng_text: Animals are made of many cells. They eat things and digest them inside. Most animals can move.

eng_text: If you look at living things under a microscope, you will see that they are made of small squares or balls.

eng_text: You can mark the passing of time yourself by observing the repetition of a cyclical event. A cyclical event is something that happens again and again regularly.

text: Waatijan na siyɛkili kɔnɔntɔnan ani muganan kɔrɔ, da kun kɛleno ala ko Nouvelle Zelande sigibaw fɔlɔ kun ye Maori ye, minunw kun be kɔnɔ belebeleba faga nin o wele ko moas.
eng_text: For a long time during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, it was believed the first inhabitants of New Zealand were the Maori people, who hunted giant birds called moas.

text: O hakilina in ye tuguni hakilina do bilasen kan ko Maoriw bɔra Polynesie batɔn ba la ani ka Nouvelle Zelande minɛ kabɔ Moriori, ka sɛnɛla dugu dɔ sigi.
eng_text: The theory then established the idea that the Maori people migrated from Polynesia in a Great Fleet and took New Zealand from the Moriori, establishing an agricultural society.

text: Nka, pirewu kura y'a jira ko Morioriw kun ye Maori gɛlɛkan mɔgɔw ye minunw bɔra Nouvelle Zelande ka ta Chatham gun sanfɛ, nin u yɛrɛ ka sɛnɛcogo lafiyalen dilani ye.
eng_text: However, new evidence suggests that the Moriori were a group of mainland Maori who migrated from New Zealand to the Chatham Islands, developing their own distinctive, peaceful culture.

text: Mɔgɔw minunw sen kun dɔneno ala san tani camaw tɛmɛni kɔ y'an dɛmɛ k'anw ka fagan ani kanu kanu nin gɛlɛlyaw  ani dɛsɛliw sɛgɛsɛgɛli ɲuman ye.
eng_text: Individuals who had been involved for several decades helped us appreciate our strengths and passions while candidly assessing difficulties and even failures.

text: Nin mɔgɔw yɛrɛ tɔgɔla tarikuw, du ani baarakɛyɔrɔ tarikuw lamɛli ye, anw be kunafoni ɲafan ma sɔrɔ kunu kan ani mɔgɔ kodɔnlen dɔ kan minunw baarakɛyɔrɔ tabolo ɛnfiliyanse sira ɲuman walima sira jugu fɛ.
eng_text: While listening to individuals share their individual, family, and organizational stories, we gained valuable insight into the past and some of the personalities who influenced for good or ill the culture of the organization.

eng_text: While understanding one’s history does not assume understanding of culture, it does at least help people gain a sense of where they fall within the history of the organization.

text: Nin taɲɛw sɛgɛsɛgɛli ye ani jantolila bɛnw na, mɔgɔw ani minunw bɛ sendɔn leno alo be bɔ kosɛbɛ baarakɛyɔrɔ tabiya, kuntilennaw ani fagan kalama.
eng_text: While assessing the successes and becoming aware of failures, individuals and the whole of the participating persons discover more deeply the values, mission, and driving forces of the organization.

text: O yɔrɔ in na, mirilila kunu antirepirɛniya tabolo ani u folola taɲɛ minunw na be mɔgɔw dɛmɛ ka dayɛlɛ yɛlɛmaliye ani tabolo kuraw o yɔrɔ ɛgilizi la.
eng_text: In this instance, recalling previous instances of entrepreneurial behavior and resulting successes helped people to be open to new changes and new direction for the local church.

text: O taɲɛ tariku in be yɛlɛmali jɔrɔ dɔgɔya, nin tabolo ɲuman natili ye ka ɲɛsin sinin yɛlɛmali ma.
eng_text: Such success stories lessened the fears of change, while creating positive inclinations toward change in the future.

text: Mwĩcirĩrie mwega nĩ urĩa urongoreirio guetha kĩhonia kia kũrehe mĩciirĩrie ĩtiganĩte hamwe nĩgũo gwetha kĩhonia.
eng_text: Convergent thinking patterns are problem solving techniques that unite different ideas or fields to find a solution.

text: ũndũ ũrĩa waarĩ na bata mwĩcirĩrie inĩ wari ihenya, ũũgĩ na kwaga kuhĩtia, hamwe na kumenya ma, kũhũthĩra njĩra ĩria ciothe ciiho hamwe na kũmaatha moohoro.
eng_text: The focus of this mindset is speed, logic and accuracy, also identification of facts, reapplying existing techniques, gathering information.

text: ũndũ ũrĩa wa bata mũno mwĩcirĩrie-ini ũyũ: Gũkorago na kĩhonia kĩmwe: Wĩchirie ũhoro wa ihonia igĩrĩ, wega kana ũru.
eng_text: The most important factor of this mindset is: there is only one correct answer. You only think of two answers, namely right or wrong.

text: Mwĩcirĩrie wa mũthemba ũyũ ukuruhanĩte na maũndũ magainie na gĩthomo kĩa sayansi haamwe na miĩkie mĩtĩkĩrĩku ya maũndũ.
eng_text: This type of thinking is associated with certain science or standard procedures.

text: Andũ arĩa makorago na mwĩcirĩrie ta ũcio nĩmahotaga kũririkana mĩtaratara, kũona ihonia na kũruta wĩra kũringana na ithimi cia sayansi.
eng_text: People with this type of thinking have logical thinking, are able to memorize patterns, solve problems and work on scientific tests.

text: Adamadenw de ye dantanfɛnw ye minunw de be seka mɔgɔ wɛrɛw hakilinaw kalan.
eng_text: Humans are by far the most talented species in reading the minds of others.

text: O kɔrɔ ye k'anw be seka ɲɛfɔ jogojɛlen na adamaden tɔw be min ye, kaniya, damina, dɔn  walima fɛ.
eng_text: That means we are able to successfully predict what other humans perceive, intend, believe, know or desire.

text: O se ninunw cɛra, mɔgɔ wɛrɛw kaniya famuyali nafan ka bɔn kosɛbɛ. A b'a t'anw be adamaden ko dogoninw dɔw ɲɛnɛbɔ.
eng_text: Among these abilities, understanding the intention of others is crucial. It allows us to resolve possible ambiguities of physical actions.

text: Misalila, nin kun ye mɔgɔ dɔ ye ka mɔbili dɔw witiri ci, i kun bena bisigi k'a be ɲinin ka wali mɔbili suyɛn.
eng_text: For example, if you were to see someone breaking a car window, you would probably assume he was trying to steal a stranger’s car.

text: A kun bena jalaki cogoya wɛrɛ la nin a kun ka mɔbili kilew ben na ani a kun y'a yɛrɛ ka mɔbili ye a kun beka min ɲinin ka kari.
eng_text: He would need to be judged differently if he had lost his car keys and it was his own car that he was trying to break into.

text: MRI sinsinleno piziki fenomɛni kan min be wele nikilerɛri makan bɔlen ye (NMR), min kodɔn na san ba 1930 kɔnɔ Felix Bloch fɛ (be baara kɛ Stanford Sanfɛkalansola) ani Edward Purcell (Kabɔ Harvard Sanfɛkalansola).
eng_text: MRI is based on a physics phenomenon called nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), which was discovered in the 1930s by Felix Bloch (working at Stanford University) and Edward Purcell (from Harvard University).

text: Nin ni makan ye, ɛman foro and aradiyo jikuruw be seka to atomuw be siɲali fitiniw di.
eng_text: In this resonance, magnetic field and radio waves cause atoms to give off tiny radio signals.

text: San ba 1970 kɔnɔn Raymond damadian, dɔkɔtɔrɔ ani dɔni ɲɛɲilikɛra dɔw,  ye ja dili ni makan ye ju dɔn inafɔ dɔkɔtɔrɔ sɛgɛsɛglikɛ baara minɛ.
eng_text: In the year 1970, Raymond Damadian, a medical doctor and research scientist, discovered the basis for using magnetic resonance imaging as a tool for medical diagnosis.

text: San naani kɔfɛ tiyiga sɛbɛn dɔ dir'ama min kun diɲɛ tigiya sɛbɛn fɔlɔ dilile ye MRI domɛni kɔnɔ.
eng_text: Four years later a patent was granted, which was the world's first patent issued in the field of MRI.

text: San ba 1977, Dɔkitɛri Damadian ye "farikolo fɔlɔ" dilani dafan, MRI sɛgɛsɛgɛlikɛna, a ye min wele ko "bukɔbali".
eng_text: In 1977, Dr. Damadian completed the construction of the first “whole-body” MRI scanner, which he called the ”Indomitable”.

text: Kuma fɔnfɔni ye ɲɔgɔnkɔ be mirili waati nege naati ani kumali tɔw fɛ.
eng_text: Asynchronous communication encourages time for reflection and reaction to others.

text: A b'a to kalandenw be se sɔrɔ ka baara kɛ  u yɛrɛ bɛrɛla ani kalan kunafoni konturolila u bɛrɛla.
eng_text: It allows students the ability to work at their own pace and control the pace of instructional information.

text: Farakan fɔlen na, waatidɔwla balelenw beyi nin baarakɛwaati yɛlɛmali cogoya dɔ ye (Bremer, 1998).
eng_text: In addition, there are fewer time restrictions with the possibility of flexible working hours. (Bremer, 1998)

text: Ɛntɛrɛnɛti itilizeli ani Diɲɛ Ɛrezoba Tugunlen siraw b'a to kalandenw be akisɛ sɔrɔ kunafonina waatibɛɛla.
eng_text: The use of the Internet and the World Wide Web allows learners to have access to information at all times.

text: Kalandenw be seka ɲininkaliw kɛ fɛnɛ kalanfaw la tile waatibɛɛla ani be sigi nin jaabi sɔrɔli ye teliyala, nin kɔnɔnilikɛli ye fo ɲɔgɔnɲe wɛrɛ ɲɔgɔnkunbɛla.
eng_text: Students can also submit questions to instructors at any time of day and expect reasonably quick responses, rather than waiting until the next face-to-face meeting.

text: Posimodɛrini mɔgɔw ka fɛrɛ kalan kuna be libɛrite di kabɔ dɔni yɛlɛmabaliw ma.
eng_text: The postmodern approach to learning offers the freedom from absolutes. There is no one good way to learn.

text: Tiɲɛla, fɛn kelen dɔrɔn teyi ka kalan. Kalan be kɛ kalanden ani dɔni jira ɲɔgɔncɛlala.
eng_text: In fact, there is not one good thing to learn.Learning takes place in the experience between the learner and the knowledge presented.

text: Anw ka yeta nin fɛɛ bɛk'i yɛrɛ ani dɔni jiralen ye, kalan kɛli jabaranin porogaramuw fɛ b'o misali jira.
eng_text: Our current experience with all the do-it-yourself and information presenting, learning-based television shows illustrates this point.

text: Anw camaw b'anw yɛrɛ ye jabarani porogaramu lajɛma min b'a kunafoni cogow walima fɛnw anw tɛna sen dɔn mina walima min dɔni bilasenkan.
eng_text: So many of us find ourselves watching a television show that informs us of a process or experience in which we will never participate or apply that knowledge.

text: Anw tɛna seka mɔbili gɛn ka minɛ fiyɛnw fiyɛnw, ka fɔntɛni dilan anw ka sokɛnɛna, ka ta Peru ka yɔrɔkɔrɔw tɔw kalan, walima anw sigiɲɔgɔn ka so dilan ye tuguni.
eng_text: We will never overhaul a car, build a fountain in our backyard, travel to Peru to examine ancient ruins, or remodel our neighbour's house.

text: Nin kɔkɔjiduguma ɛntɛrɛnɛti filijuruw ye, fili dugulen Erɔpula ani satelitibaw la, Greenland tugulen na kaɲɛ nin u yɔrɔ mɔgɔ 93 kɛmɛ sarala akisɛsɔrɔli ɛntɛrɛnɛti la.
eng_text: Thanks to undersea fiber optic cable links to Europe and broadband satellite, Greenland is well connected with 93% of the population having internet access.

text: I ka otɛli walima jiginyɔrɔ (Nin be ka to dunajiginso kɔnɔ walima yɛrɛtɔgɔla so) bena seka lala wifi walima ɔridinatɛri konɛkitenin sɔrɔ, abi ɛntɛrɛnɛti sɔrɔ bɔn be sigida bɛɛ la walima jamana wifi yɔrɔ dɔw la.
eng_text: Your hotel or hosts (if staying in a guesthouse or private home) will likely have wifi or an internet connected PC, and all settlements have an internet cafe or some location with public wifi.

text: Ota ũria hekũgwetetwo hau kabere, ona korwo kiugo "Eskimo" nĩgĩtĩkĩrĩtwo bũrũrinĩ wa United States, nĩgĩkuagwo rĩnaihũthia kũrĩ andũ a Arctic arĩa matarĩ a bũrũri wa U.S, mũno mũno Canada.
eng_text: As mentioned above, though the word "Eskimo" remains acceptable in the United States, it is considered pejorative by many non-U.S. Arctic peoples, especially in Canada.

text: Ona waigua kiugo kĩu gĩkĩhũthĩrwo nĩ aikari a Greenland, ũhũthĩrĩ wa kĩo niwagĩirwo gũithemwo nĩ oki.
eng_text: While you may hear the word used by Greenlandic Natives, its use should be avoided by foreigners.

text: Aikari ambere a Greenland meĩtaga Inuit bũrũrinĩ wa Canada na Kalaalleq (uingĩ kalaallit) Greenlander thĩini wa Greenland.
eng_text: The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland.

text: Fagali ani nkɛniɲɛ juguya ka ɲɛsin dunanw ma bakurubafɔlila, ma dɔn fɔlɔ Greenland kɔnɔ. Ali duguw kɔɔnɔ, "yɔrɔ jugumaw" foyi si tey.
eng_text: Crime, and ill-will toward foreigners in general, is virtually unknown in Greenland. Even in the towns, there are no "rough areas."

text: Nɛnɛ waati de ye lala farati yɛrɛ yɛrɛ min bena mɔgɔ labɛnlen baliw sɛgɛn.
eng_text: Cold weather is perhaps the only real danger the unprepared will face.

text: Nin i be Greeland lajɛ nɛnɛ waatiw la (Jateminɛna i be ka kɔkɔdugu yanfan fɛ cogomina, nɛnɛ be juguya o cogo kelen na), a nafan ka bɔn kana ni fini futeni dama damaniw ye.
eng_text: If you visit Greenland during cold seasons (considering that the further north you go, the colder it will be), it is essential to bring warm enough clothing.

text: Tile janba tilema fɛ be seka sunɔkɔbaliya kaɲɛ kunbalan nati ani kɛnɛya kunbalanw.
eng_text: The very long days in the summer can lead to problems getting sufficient sleep and associated health issues.

text: Tilema waatila, janto fɛnɛ Nordique sosow la. Ali na sɔrɔ u tɛ bana foyisi yɛlɛma, u be seka tɔrɔlikɛ.
eng_text: During the summer, also watch out for the Nordic mosquitoes. Although they do not transmit any diseases, they can be irritating.

text: Ali na sɔrɔ San Francisco sɔrɔ sirileno o la nin o ye diɲɛ lajɛlikɛyɔrɔ ba ye, a sɔrɔda ka ca.
eng_text: While San Francisco's economy is linked to it being a world-class tourist attraction, its economy is diversified.

text: Baarakɛbɔnda min be mɔgɔ camaw ta barala ye sɛriwisiw ye, gofɛrɛnema, waaribaarayɔrɔw, jako ani turisimu.
eng_text: The largest employment sectors are professional services, government, finance, trade, and tourism.

text: Waatila dɔngili, filimuw ani sɛbɛeniw ɲɛfɔli ani tabolo kodɔnlen y'a dugu dɛmɛ ka ɲɛnɛmaya ani a tamasiyɛnw dɔnlen diɲɛ fanbɛɛ.
eng_text: Its frequent portrayal in music, films, literature and popular culture has helped make the city and its landmarks known throughout the world.

text: San Francisco ye turusi infirasirikiti ba camaw dilan nin ɔtɛli camaw ye, dugunikɛyɔrɔw, ani yɔrɔbaw minunw be diɲɛ yɔrɔbaw jɔcogo bato.
eng_text: San Francisco has developed a large tourist infrastructure with numerous hotels, restaurants, and top-notch convention facilities.

text: San Francisco ye fɛnɛ jamana yɔrɔba dɔ ye nin Asie dumuniw ye: Koree, Thailande, Inde ani Japon dumuniw.
eng_text: San Francisco is also one of the best places in the nation for other Asian cuisine: Korean, Thai, Indian, and Japanese.

text: Woyazi kɛɛli ka ta Walt Disney World la be ejita bele jira Ameriki du camaw fɛ.
eng_text: Traveling to Walt Disney World represents a major pilgrimage for many American families.

text: Lajɛli "tigitigi" ye ka pan ka Orlando ayeropɔru la, ka bisi ta ka o yɔrɔ Disney ɔtɛli, ka dugunu fila ɲɔgɔna kɛ yani kabɔ Disney dugu kɔnɔn ani ka segin so.
eng_text: The "typical" visit involves flying into Orlando International Airport, busing to an on-site Disney hotel, spending about a week without leaving Disney property, and returning home.

text: Yɛlɛmali cama cogoya wɛrɛw beyi, nka in de ye mɔgɔ camaw kan bɛ min ma nin u kumana "taali kan Disney World kɔnɔ".
eng_text: There are infinite variations possible, but this remains what most people mean when they talk of "going to Disney World".

text: Tike camaw be fere ɛntɛrɛnɛti sanfɛ ferelikɛsitiw kan inafɔ eBay walima Craigslist dɔn cama pariki tike tikɛni finitiw itilize.
eng_text: Many tickets sold online through auction websites such as eBay or Craigslist are partially used multi-day park-hopper tickets.

text: Ali ni o ye baara kodɔnlen ba dɔ ye, a kɔn neno Disney fɛ: tikew tɛ seka yɛlɛma.
eng_text: While this is a very common activity, it is prohibited by Disney: the tickets are non-transferable.

text: Camping oyothe rungu wa rim ya Grand Canyon nĩĩrabatara marũa ma backcountry.
eng_text: Any camping below the rim in Grand Canyon requires a backcountry permit.

text: Marua cinyihagĩo kũgitĩra Canyon na cionekaga kuma mũthenya wa 1 wa mweri, mĩeri ĩna mbere ya mweri wa kwanjia.
eng_text: Permits are limited to protect the canyon, and become available on the 1st day of the month, four months prior to the start month.

text: Nĩkĩo marũa ma backcountry mweri-inĩ wa gatano monekanaga mweri ĩmwe mweri-inĩ wa mũgaa.
eng_text: Thus, a backcountry permit for any start date in May becomes available on 1 Jan.

text: Nabaathi cia matũra marĩa moĩkaine, ta Bright Angel Campground ĩrĩa ĩ hakanĩtie na Phantom Ranch, ihũragio nĩ mahoya ma mũthenya wa mbere kũhingũrwo.
eng_text: Space for the most popular areas, such as the Bright Angel Campground adjacent to Phantom Ranch, generally fill up by the requests received on first date they are opened to reservations.

text: Kwĩna marũa nini cĩa kũingĩra na magũrũ ĩrĩa ciheanagwo kũrĩ a mbere gũkinya.
eng_text: There are a limited number permits reserved for walk-in requests available on a first come, first served basis.

text: Dɔnila Farafina Wɔrɔdugu yanfan fɛ mɔbilila ye cogoya ɲuman ba ye k'o maraw cɛnan ye ani ka se yɔrɔw la minunw tɛ kɛ turisiw tɛmɛ siraw la.
eng_text: Entering Southern Africa by car is an amazing way to see all the region's beauty as well as to get to places off the normal tourist routes.

text: UO be seka kɛ mɔbili gansan kɔnɔ nin bolodali ɲuman kli ye nka mɔbili 4 x 4 de laɲini neno kosɛbɛ ani yɔrɔ camaw be sɔrɔ nin mɔbili  4 x 4 sen jan ba dɔ ye.
eng_text: This can be done in a normal car with careful planning but a 4x4 is highly advised and many locations are only accessible with a high wheel base 4x4.

text: A bil'i kun na bolodaliwaatila ko ali na sɔrɔ Sud-Afiriki suma neno, a gɛrɛfɛ jamanaw bɛ tɛ.
eng_text: Keep in mind while planning that although Southern Africa is stable not all neighboring countries are.

text: Visa ɲininfɛnw an'a sɔngɔn be yɛlɛma kabɔ jamanaw dɔ la ka ta jamana dɔ la ani be ɛnfiliyanse nin i beka jamana mina ye.
eng_text: Visa requirements and costs vary from nation to nation and are affected by the country you come from.

text: Jamana kelenw kelenw ka sariya kɛrɛnkɛrɛni fɛnɛ beyi min jatogola yɛrɛdɛmɛ fɛnw minunw kan ka kɛ mɔbili kɔnɔ.
eng_text: Each country also has unique laws requiring what emergency items need to be in the car.

text: Voctoria Falls ye dugu ye Zimbabwe worodugu yanfan fɛ, furɔntiyɛri la nin Livingstone, Zambie, ani Botswana gɛrɛfɛ.
eng_text: Victoria Falls is a town in the western portion of Zimbabwe, across the border from Livingstone, Zambia, and near Botswana.

text: Dugu dalen no masurunyala jibɔn yɔrɔwɔ gɛrɛfɛ, ani u de ye samani kɛrɛyɔrɔ ba ye, nka nin lajɛli yɔrɔ kodɔnlen ba be toli kuntagala jan opɔritinite di layalikɛlaw ani lajɛlikɛlaw ma.
eng_text: The town lies immediately next to the falls, and they are the major attraction, but this popular tourist destination offers both adventure seekers and sightseers plenty of opportunities for a longer stay.

text: Samiya waatil kɔnɔ (Nowanburukalo ka Marisikalo), ji bɔnɲa be yɛlɛ ani jibɔnyɔrɔ bena cɛn kojuguya.
eng_text: In the rainy season (November to March), the water volume will be higher and the Falls will be more dramatic.

text: Sikatala i be ɲiki nin ye pɔn tikɛ walima tamana sirafitiniw fɛ minunw be jibɔnyɔrɔ gɛrɛfɛ.
eng_text: You are guaranteed to get wet if you cross the bridge or walk along the trails winding near the Falls.

text: Sira wɛrɛ fɛ, o de kama tiki tiki bari ji bɔnɲa yɛlɛneno kosɛbɛ ko ji bɔnw yɔrɔ lajɛli be dibi - nin jiw bɛɛ ye.
eng_text: On the other hand, it is precisely because the volume of water is so high that your viewing of the actual Falls will be obscured—by all the water!
